- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak or use lagged mean.
- If model forecast is significantly below recent 5-day average, consider mean reversion bias — increase forecast toward historical mean.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.33), model often fails to capture momentum; use sentiment-weighted moving average or median of recent 7-day forecast.
- If true outcome is consistently higher than forecast in 3–5 consecutive days, model may be under-reacting to bullish sentiment — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending, model often lags — forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of true price if sentiment is flat or mildly bullish.
